title: Democratizing AI: Open-source Scalable LLM Training on GPU-based Supercomputers
problem: Training LLMs with hundreds of billions to trillions of parameters requires tens of thousands of GPUs and a highly scalable software stack to achieve sufficient throughput. At scale, models suffer from catastrophic memorization in a single pass, causing disclosure of sensitive training data.
motivation: Making LLM training accessible on supercomputers while preventing privacy and copyright risks from memorization inherent to large-scale training.
method: AxoNN implements a four-dimensional hybrid parallel algorithm with optimized matrix multiply kernels and overlapped non-blocking collectives. Performance modeling selects optimal configurations per supercomputer, and techniques prevent catastrophic memorization by limiting model capacity to forget training data.
key_novelty: Four-dimensional hybrid parallelism achieving unprecedented Exascale throughput on GPU supercomputers with integrated defenses against catastrophic memorization.
contributions: AxoNN open-source framework for scalable LLM training
Four-dimensional hybrid parallel algorithm for GPT-style transformers
Performance optimizations for kernel execution and collective communication overlap
Methods to prevent catastrophic memorization in large models

metrics.other: Peak throughput: 1.423 Exaflop/s (bf16, Alps), 1.381 Exaflop/s (bf16, Frontier), 620.1 Petaflop/s (bf16, Perlmutter)

limitations: Limitations of the approach are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Scalable distributed training for large language models
